notes: Diff is 2 files, 22 added lines, no deletions: webapp/tsconfig.json gains "types": ["vite/client"], plus a new guard test webapp/src/tsconfig.test.ts. No scope creep, no refactors, no dependency changes, no server/auth/migration/secret code touched.

Reproduced the bug the commit message describes. An ancestor directory of this worktree really does carry /home/hkjang/node_modules/@types/node. Running tsc with main's tsconfig (types field absent) fails: src/features/workspace/composer/useDraft.test.tsx(196,76) TS2345 'Type number is not assignable to type Timeout'. With the pinned field, tsc --noEmit exits 0. The fix does exactly what the message claims.

Verified the claim 'src references no Node globals': grep for process./__dirname/Buffer/NodeJS./require( across webapp/src returns nothing. vite.config.ts does use node:path, but tsconfig include is ["src"], so it was never in the program and is unaffected by the pin.
Full webapp suite passes: 45 files / 189 tests, and tsc --noEmit exits 0 on HEAD.

The new test is not a no-op. Before the change compilerOptions.types is absent, so expect(types).toEqual(["vite/client"]) fails at runtime (and the property access would not even typecheck). It does verify the change, though it is a config-mirror assertion rather than a behavioral one: it locks the field's value but cannot catch a regression that reintroduces ambient @types by another route (a transitive /// <reference types="node" /> in a dependency's .d.ts still bypasses compilerOptions.types). A stronger guard would be a CI typecheck run with @types/node deliberately present in an ancestor node_modules. Not blocking.
webapp/src/tsconfig.test.ts:19 'expect(types).not.toContain("node")' is fully subsumed by the toEqual on line 15. Redundant, harmless.

Maintenance note: with types pinned, any future global type package (vitest globals, @testing-library/jest-dom matchers) must be added in two places, tsconfig.json and this test, or the suite goes red. That is the intended trade-off, just worth knowing.
Reversibility is trivial: config-only, no data migration, no external state, no generated artifacts committed (webapp/dist and tsconfig.tsbuildinfo untouched).
